plan.change: Phase C follow-up: fail closed on invalid UTF-8 Git pathname bytes
expectedChanges: Read Git pathname-bearing output as raw bytes and decode it with fatal UTF-8 semantics.
Fail closed before Scope/Risk/Impact evaluation when Git pathname bytes are not valid UTF-8.
Add real Git regressions for committed and untracked non-UTF-8 filenames.
hqDecisions: This change addresses only the Codex P2 invalid UTF-8 pathname-byte finding from superseded PR #30.
Valid UTF-8 Git path identity must remain literal exactly as established by the prior M2 fixes.
Invalid UTF-8 pathname bytes must not be replacement-decoded to U+FFFD; the gate must fail closed instead.
Do not address human-readable report escaping, M1, H2, L1, Record v0.3, broader Phase D/E, or production here.
rulesApplied: Codex P2 invalid UTF-8 pathname finding
plan.manualCheckExemptionReason: Change OS Git pathname decoding only; behavior is covered by real Git regression fixtures, trusted PR gate, and later canary.
plan.rollback: Revert this staging-only remediation PR; production remains untouched.
outOfScope: M1 old Change PR Gate Plan Lock parity
H2 staging branch protection and required checks
Phase D broader Git/index hardening beyond this exact decoding defect
Phase E semantic scope and concurrency controls
unverified: Post-fix unusual-path canary coverage remains required before C3-1 is formally closed.
plan.problem: Git permits pathname bytes that are not valid UTF-8 on POSIX, while Node string decoding with encoding utf8 replaces invalid byte sequences with U+FFFD and can collapse distinct repository identities.
plan.currentContract: collectChangedPaths uses NUL-delimited Git output but receives it through a helper configured with encoding utf8, so invalid pathname bytes are replacement-decoded before parsing.
plan.whyExistingIsInsufficient: A raw byte filename such as docs/0xFF.md can decode to the same JavaScript string as a real UTF-8 docs/�.md path, allowing deduplication or policy matching against the wrong repository identity.
plan.design: For Git commands whose stdout contains pathnames, capture stdout as Buffer, decode with TextDecoder utf-8 fatal mode, and throw a dedicated fail-closed error on invalid UTF-8 before parsing. Keep non-path Git helpers unchanged.
alternativesRejected: Silently replacement-decode invalid bytes; that preserves the identity collision.
Represent all Git paths as arbitrary byte arrays throughout every policy layer; unnecessary for the current UTF-8 project contract and substantially broadens Phase D.
Globally ban unusual valid UTF-8 filenames; prior fixes intentionally preserve valid literal Git identities.
plan.compatibility: All valid UTF-8 Git pathname output keeps the same literal string semantics. Only invalid UTF-8 pathnames now stop verification.
boundaryCases: A committed filename containing raw 0xFF must cause collectChangedPaths to fail closed.
An untracked filename containing raw 0xFF must cause worktree collection to fail closed.
A valid UTF-8 filename containing U+FFFD remains a valid distinct pathname and must not itself be rejected.
Existing Unicode, tab, newline, backslash and quote filenames remain supported.
testPlan: Create a temporary real Git repository with a filename containing raw invalid UTF-8 byte 0xFF and commit it; assert collectChangedPaths throws the fail-closed error.
Create an untracked raw-byte invalid UTF-8 filename and assert worktree collection throws the same error.
Keep existing valid UTF-8 unusual-path regression tests green.
Run Change Operations regression suite, trusted Change PR Gate, and Change Verification Evidence.
plan.promotionRisk: Staging Change OS only. Incorrect decoding behavior could over-allow or falsely reject changes, so trusted gate review and canary are required.
